author: Felipe Maschio
html:
Fair challenge — JEP 491 was a big deal, and the article’s own advice is that upgrading is the single best fix available. Two reasons I’d push back on “basically irrelevant”, though:

1. What 491 removed is the monitor case. Blocking inside a native call (JNI/FFM) still pins today, on 24 and 25 alike. And that’s not theoretical: Pi4J merged a fix for exactly this a few months ago — virtual threads doing a blocking native poll() pinned all four carriers on a Raspberry Pi 4, so digital inputs 5+ simply never fired (Pi4J/pi4j#623). The fix was moving that path back to platform threads.

2. Adoption reality: most production JVMs I get to see are still on 21, and plenty on 17. For every team already on 25, several more will be reading 21-era thread dumps well into 2027. “Upgrade” is the right advice — “irrelevant” assumes everyone already took it.

So: less relevant than in 2024? Absolutely, and the article says so. Basically irrelevant? Tell that to the 5th button on that Raspberry Pi.
